market.state: UPTREND INTACT - BROAD GIVE-BACK, REAL ASSETS THE ONLY BID
market.advice: The index held and almost everything underneath it slipped. SPY closed at 762.78, down about 0.8%, 1.9% off its high but still comfortably above a rising 50-day at 750.72 with the distribution-day count at zero, so the trend structure is untouched. The internals are a different story. QQQ closed at 710.93, down 0.7%, and is now BELOW its 50-day for the first time in this leg. Breadth fell from 57% to 51% of the 474 scanned names above their 50-day, VIX ticked up to 16.0 against a 15.2 five-day average, and the signal migration was decisively one-sided: 65 names downgraded, only 26 upgraded, leaving 152 STRONG BUY, 144 WATCH and 178 WEAK. Nine of eleven sectors closed red. This is not damage, it is narrowing - and narrowing is what you manage, not what you panic about. What actually happened is that yesterday's two big trades were both partly unwound. Healthcare, which averaged +5.4% yesterday, gave back -1.6% today, and the giveback was concentrated exactly where the froth was: MRNA -23.5% after Tuesday's +177% vaccine spike, ISRG -5.8%, BSX -5.1%, SYK -3.6%. If you did not chase Moderna, this cost you nothing, which is the whole point. Banks kept falling for a second session - Financial Services -0.9% with COF -3.7%, SYF -3.6%, LNC -3.5% - so yesterday's read that lower yields hand you a risk-defined entry in the highest-scoring banks has NOT worked yet. JPM still scores 92.2 with an RSI of 50.3, but TradingView rates it a flat NEUTRAL at 8 buy / 10 neutral / 8 sell, and two down days in a row on the group means the pullback is still a pullback and not yet a base. That is marked WATCH rather than STRONG BUY for exactly that reason. Consumer took a real hit: WMT fell 9.2% on 3.31x average volume on its earnings print, COTY -9.6%, and Consumer Cyclical was the second-worst sector at -1.6%. Three groups closed green and all three are real assets. Basic Materials led at +0.7%, driven by an agricultural complex that woke up on Deere's earnings - DE +6.9% on 2.54x volume, CF +5.6%, MOS +5.0%, BG +2.2%, with CTVA upgrading off the bottom. FCX +3.1% printed a new 52-week high and gold followed (NEM +2.1%). Energy added +0.5% and remains the single best group in the market, converting 15 of 20 names to STRONG BUY - 75%, unchanged and still the highest on the board - with COP +3.3%, OXY +2.4%, DVN +2.3%, APA +2.2%, EOG +1.8%, TRGP +1.8%, LNG +1.8%. The catalyst is not technical: Bessent said the US will impose its toughest-ever sanctions on Iran and pressed China to cooperate, the Houthis struck Najran airport and Aramco facilities inside Saudi Arabia, a tanker off Yemen was boarded and diverted toward Somalia, and Aramco is now selling cargoes that load outside Hormuz. Supply risk is escalating, not resolving. Real Estate scraped +0.1% on data-center strength (ARE +4.7%). The one bright spot in technology was memory and networking silicon bouncing off deeply oversold levels - MRVL +5.8%, MU +4.0%, STX +2.1% - but the semicap group did not participate (AMAT flat, KLAC -0.8%, AMAT still -31% from its high), so treat the bounce as a bounce until semicap confirms. Cybersecurity kept bleeding (CRWD -5.6%, ZS -5.2%). Sector conversion into the next session reads Energy 75%, Basic Materials 58%, Healthcare 42%, Industrials 36%, Consumer Defensive 34%, Financials 32%, Technology 28%, Consumer Cyclical 25%, Real Estate 18%, Communication Services 17% and Utilities 9%. How to trade it: keep normal position sizing, because the index has not given a single distribution day and sits above a rising 50-day. But buy where the money is actually going rather than where it left. Energy and materials are the only groups where price, breadth and a live external catalyst all point the same way, and inside energy the correct choice is the least-extended name, not the highest score - APA is 23.6% above its 50-day and MPC 21.5% above, which is why both are WATCH here despite scores of 92 and 93. Do not buy the healthcare giveback yet; the two names that led yesterday are the two that hurt most today. Leave semicap alone until the group stops making lower lows. And respect the calendar - the next fifteen sessions carry a dense earnings cluster (SJM 6 days, then NVDA, CRM, A, DLTR and CRWD at 7, MRVL, WDAY and RBRK at 8, SAIC 11, PANW and DELL 13, NTAP, SNOW, CPB and HPE 14). NVDA reports in seven days and it is the whole market's binary event, which is why a 90.7-score name with 214% EPS growth and a 16.7x forward multiple is on the watch list instead of the buy list.
